title: Rosewater Lane Rising
premise: Quentin Villalobos, keeper of the Rosewater Lane lighthouse and a stalled romance novelist, finds an undelivered letter his grandfather wrote eleven years ago — addressed to the man Quentin loved and abandoned to protect the family vineyard's reputation. When that man, Elias Marrow, returns as the lawyer overseeing the vineyard's contested estate, Quentin must choose between confessing the truth and preserving the fragile peace he's built. As the first harvest approaches, Quentin forgives himself, delivers the letter at last, and chooses love over duty, ending with the two of them watching the lighthouse beam sweep the ripe vines.
about_author: Q. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing undelivered letters in coastal post offices. They write romances about people who mistake duty for destiny.

chapters.title: The Undelivered
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sorting his late grandfather's belongings in the lighthouse, Quentin finds a sealed, yellowed letter postmarked eleven years ago — addressed to Elias Marrow. He recognizes the name and freezes, memories flooding back. Emotional beat: dread and denial, the past knocking on a door Quentin boarded shut.

chapters.title: Postscript to a Coward
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with a flashback to eleven years prior. We learn Quentin ended things with Elias to shield the Villalobos vineyard from scandal, then wrote himself into silence as a novelist instead. He burns dinner, can't write, rereads the letter without opening it. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into avoidance.

chapters.title: The Lawyer at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias arrives in town as counsel for the trust contesting the vineyard's ownership — older, composed, unreadable. He and Quentin meet at the property line, all professional courtesy and old electricity. Emotional beat: tension of unfinished business disguised as legal formality.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Forced to work alongside Elias cataloguing the vineyard's records for the case, Quentin discovers his grandfather's letters hint at a secret the family kept — one that explains the scandal Quentin sacrificed his love to hide. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything Quentin believed.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands Quentin and Elias in the lighthouse overnight. Old intimacy resurfaces in small gestures — coffee made the right way, a blanket offered without words. They nearly talk about the past; they don't. Emotional beat: warmth rekindled and immediately feared.

chapters.title: The Trust's Terms
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias uncovers evidence that could win the case — and destroy the Villalobos family, revealing his employers want more than the vineyard. He realizes Quentin's grandfather's letter may hold the key. Emotional beat: duty and desire pulling in opposite directions, Elias now the one torn.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finally opens the letter and learns his grandfather confessed the family's secret to Elias years ago — and Elias never used it. Quentin's sacrifice was built on a lie he told himself. He confronts Elias, who admits he came back for Quentin, not the case. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Harvest Clause
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The trust moves to seize the vineyard before harvest. Elias must decide whether to submit the damning evidence or burn his career. Quentin, in turn, must decide whether to fight beside the man he wronged. Emotional beat: rising stakes, love becoming a choice rather than a feeling.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, climax. At the estate hearing, Quentin stands and delivers his grandfather's letter aloud, exposing the family secret himself and disarming the trust's claim. He publicly claims his own fault first — forgiving the man in the mirror before asking forgiveness from anyone else. Emotional beat: catharsis, courage, the truth as liberation.

chapters.title: Rosewater Lane, Rising
chapters.summary: Dual POV, resolution. The vineyard survives under new shared stewardship; Elias stays, having resigned from the trust. On the first morning of harvest, Quentin hands Elias a new letter — this one sealed, addressed, and finally deliverable: the first chapter of a novel about two men and a lighthouse. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and unhurried, love in the present tense at last.
